correctness.rationale: Exact iterate formula; fully proved finite-cardinality column rearrangement inequality for 0<beta=alpha*p<1; weak distribution follows via Tonelli and counting. The converse uses a basis orbit with s+1 comparable residual indices and the local slow-variation doubling constant. All subcritical strong exponents follow from Potter and Jensen, and failure at and above q0 follows by fixed terminal multiplicative blocks and a single maximal orbit value. Includes boundaries p=1 and all 0<alpha<1/p. Finite code diagnostics are supplementary only.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The published universal strong self-improvement threshold cannot imply a uniform weak critical statement: positive logarithmic factors preserve every subcritical strong exponent but fail the critical weak bound. Type-based weak control in Arnold concerns a smaller exponent and does not dominate the critical q0 statement. A separate published feasible-region result concerns strong q exponents.

originality.rationale: The if-and-only-if almost-decreasing criterion for all positive measurable slowly varying multipliers is absent from the inspected strong theory and the accessible pure-power weak endpoint. Exact mathematical implication comparison: the pure-power theorem only treats L=1; Abbar–Arnold–Coine treat strong q-moments; Arnold treats a strong cutoff and a Banach-type weak exponent, and none determines whether a slowly varying perturbation preserves the weak q0 endpoint. Search/primary full text inspection did not identify stronger coverage. Residual earlier alternate terminology risk persists.
residual_risks: A prior general weak-orbit theorem for regularly varying shifts under Lorentz/Marcinkiewicz or weighted-shift terminology may exist outside the inspected sources.
